content.user_title: Validate UI Changes With Visual Evidence
content.value_statement: UI changes can pass code review while still missing visual, responsive, or accessibility goals. This skill guides rigorous screenshot-based validation with measurable findings and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Reviews screenshots for visual defects, layout issues, and incomplete UI changes.
Compares stated UI goals against visible evidence from before and after states.
Checks design system alignment for color, spacing, typography, icons, and components.
Assesses visual accessibility signals such as contrast, focus indicators, and readability.
Guides visual regression workflows using tools such as Chromatic, Percy, Applitools, BackstopJS, Playwright, and Cypress.
Supports responsive, dark mode, loading state, error state, and cross-browser validation planning.
limitations: It does not include executable test code or bundled visual testing tools.
It depends on provided screenshots, design goals, or testing output for accurate review.
It cannot confirm runtime behavior without representative interactive states and environments.
Exact pixel diffs and contrast ratios may require separate measurement tools.

use_cases.title: Validate Pull Request UI Changes
use_cases.description: Review before and after screenshots to confirm a UI change meets the stated goal and has no visible regressions.

use_cases.title: Audit Design System Compliance
use_cases.description: Check components against design tokens, typography rules, spacing standards, color palettes, and icon usage.

use_cases.title: Check Accessibility Visual States
use_cases.description: Assess contrast, focus indicators, readable text, responsive layouts, loading states, and error states before release.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Screenshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this UI screenshot for visible layout, typography, spacing, color, and accessibility issues. Start with observed visual evidence, then list specific fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Before And After
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these before and after screenshots against this goal: [describe goal]. Decide whether the goal is achieved, partially achieved, or not achieved.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Responsive Accessibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate these desktop, tablet, and mobile screenshots for responsive behavior, visual hierarchy, contrast, focus visibility, and error or loading states.

prompt_templates.title: Design A Regression Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a visual validation plan for this component library using screenshot review, regression testing, accessibility checks, and pull request review gates.

output_examples.input: A before and after screenshot of a redesigned checkout button.
output_examples.output: From the visual evidence, the button is larger and easier to scan, but the disabled state is not shown. The color contrast should be measured before approval.

output_examples.input: Mobile screenshots of a navigation menu after a responsive update.
output_examples.output: The menu collapses at the expected width, but the active item loses its visual state. The focus indicator is also too subtle on dark backgrounds.

output_examples.input: Screenshots of a form with validation errors and loading states.
output_examples.output: The error text is visible and close to each field, but the loading state shifts the submit button. Reserve stable space to prevent layout movement.

best_practices: Provide clear goals, before and after screenshots, and the target viewport sizes.
Validate key states, including hover, focus, disabled, loading, error, empty, and dark mode.
Pair visual review with measurement tools for pixel diffs, contrast ratios, and cross-browser coverage.
anti_patterns: Declaring a UI change successful from code changes without visual evidence.
Testing only one desktop screenshot for a responsive or cross-platform feature.
Ignoring focus, contrast, loading, error, and empty states during visual review.

faq.question: Does this skill run visual tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides expert guidance for analysis and workflow design, but separate tools must capture screenshots or run tests.

faq.question: Which visual testing tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It references Chromatic, Percy, Applitools, BackstopJS, Playwright visual comparisons, Cypress visual testing, and Jest image snapshots.

faq.question: Can it review accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on visual accessibility signals such as contrast, focus indicators, readability, hierarchy, and responsive behavior.

faq.question: What input gives the best result?
faq.answer: Use before and after screenshots, target goals, viewport details, theme information, and any known design system rules.

faq.question: Can it replace human design review?
faq.answer: No. It structures visual QA and highlights issues, but product context and final design judgment still matter.

faq.question: Is it useful for pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can help reviewers verify visible UI changes, document regressions, and request specific remediation before merge.
